source.name: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

method: Additive source-specific morphology extracted from printed regional flora; no changes to existing species cards, image credits, BONAP or website. Secondary treatments flagged, not automatically adopted.

morphology.habit: Gray soft-pubescent taprooted annual; to 50 cm
morphology.leaves: Genus: alternate, narrowing into petiolar bases, linear to oblong-oblanceolate; entire to pinnately lobed
morphology.heads: Rather large; involucres 6–8 mm high and 7–13 mm wide
morphology.rays: 20–44; ligules 8–15 mm, white with reddish/rosy streaks beneath
morphology.discs: Yellow per genus treatment; disk corolla bases swell and harden at maturity per species key
morphology.pappus: Minute, 0.25–1 mm; key describes uneven crown of ca. five acute scales
morphology.habitat: Sandy open woods, fields, prairies and roadsides

source_disagreements: Compare A. riddellii: latter perennial from woody roots with 40–85 rays and pappus ≤0.2 mm.

records.flora_original_name: Artemisia ludoviciana Nutt. subsp. mexicana (Willd. ex Spreng.) D.D. Keck

morphology.leaves: Alternate; variable from entire to lobed/dissected; young leaves white woolly both sides, older upper surfaces sometimes dark green and nearly hairless while lower surface stays white woolly
morphology.involucres: Grayish to white woolly, 2.5–4+ mm high
morphology.florets: Genus: minute yellowish-white heads; ray and disk florets, disk florets fertile in the described taxon
morphology.fruits: Genus: achenes approximately ≤1 mm, pappus absent

source_disagreements: Flora's record is specifically subsp. mexicana; do not attribute all varietal characters to species-level A. ludoviciana.
Older flora claims subsp. ludoviciana absent from TX; modern regional occurrences require independent validation.

morphology.leaves: Sessile to shortly petiolate; blades punctate, upper leaves entire and lower entire to serrate, 1-nerved with obscure lateral nerves; key: linear or very narrowly elliptic, generally 2–4(–5) mm wide
morphology.heads: Dioecious, in paniculate/corymbose clusters; no rays
morphology.fruits: Achenes ca. 1.2 mm; key says 8–10 ribs; pistillate pappus 7–12 mm

source_disagreements: Pistillate plants required for definitive determination per genus treatment; compare B. salicina's 6–8 mm pistillate involucre.

morphology.leaves: Nearly sessile; serrate, wider blades 3-nerved; key: oblanceolate, 4–8(–15) mm wide
morphology.fruits: Achenes 1.2–2 mm; pistillate pappus to 12 mm
morphology.habitat: Alluvial, often sandy or saline soils

source_disagreements: Critical nomenclatural ambiguity: repository Baccharis salicifolia lacks authorship; POWO considers Baccharis salicifolia Nutt. a synonym of B. salicina but also accepts distinct Baccharis salicifolia (Ruiz & Pav.) Pers. Do not automatically equate all 'B. salicifolia' usages. Taxon-concept verification required before applying historic morphology to species card.

morphology.habit: Weakly suffrutescent perennial, stems to 1 m, can make second flush of flowering shoots after spring
morphology.leaves: 4–15 × 2–6 cm, toothed; stiff-hirsute to scabrous or loosely hairy, not velvety; central stem leaves sessile or short-petiolate; key: ovate to triangular, densely leafy
morphology.heads: 1–several in corymbose clusters; genus: green receptacular bracts and reddish-maroon disk
morphology.rays: Yellow-orange with green veins on lower surface per genus key; ligules 10.5–17 mm
morphology.fruits: Achenes 4.5–6 × 3–5 mm; pappus absent or inconspicuous per genus
morphology.habitat: Sandy soils, post oak woods and relatively open places

source_disagreements: Historic synonym Berlandiera texana DC. noted in flora; FNA instead recognizes Berlandiera ×betonicifolia as hybrid between B. pumila and B. texana. POWO accepts B. betonicifolia. Preserve competing concepts.
secondary_sources_checked: Flora of North America hybrid treatment

morphology.habit: Perennial herb, stems to 1.2 m, persistent basal rosette
morphology.leaves: Crowded near base; velvety; at least some lyrate-pinnatifid per key
morphology.heads: Genus: corymbose clusters, green receptacular bracts visible in maroon disk
morphology.rays: Yellow-orange with red/maroon veins on reverse, sometimes entire undersurface maroon; ligules 10–14 mm
morphology.fruits: Achenes 4.5–6 × 2.7–3.7 mm; pappus absent or inconspicuous per genus
morphology.habitat: Dry rocky limestone places and roadsides

source_disagreements: Contrast B. betonicifolia: lyrate basal foliage and red-maroon ray undersides rather than densely stem-leafy green-veined rays.

morphology.leaves: Opposite per genus; once pinnate/ternate, 3–5 lanceolate serrate segments; petioles 10–60 mm
morphology.heads: Outer phyllaries 5–10, linear-spatulate and conspicuously ciliate, sometimes 30–50 mm; inner phyllaries 5–7 mm
morphology.rays: Absent or tiny golden-yellow ligules 2–3.5 mm per key
morphology.fruits: Flattened wedge-shaped achenes, each face 1-nerved, 5–8(–10) × 2.5–4 mm; pappus awns 3–4.5 mm, genus typically barbed

source_disagreements: FNA fruit characters in existing species record differ by inner versus outer cypsela and possible barb orientation; retain both and do not overwrite detailed existing verification.

morphology.habit: Annual or perennial in regional flora, 0.3–1 m; life-cycle differences against modern FNA need to be tracked
morphology.leaves: Opposite; sessile, simple, linear-lanceolate or rarely narrow ovate, serrate or nearly entire
morphology.heads: Outer phyllaries 6–8, linear-lanceolate, usually not longer than head
morphology.rays: Usually 7–8, sometimes absent; golden yellow occasionally tinged red; 15–30 mm
morphology.fruits: Wedge-shaped achenes 6–9 × ca. 2 mm; pappus 2–4 retrorsely barbed awns 3–5 mm

source_disagreements: Previously corrected learner gives FNA life cycle as annual sometimes persisting; source accounts differ in framing, retain separately.

morphology.stems: Diffusely branched inflorescence, solitary heads at ends of branches
morphology.rays: 15–20 pistillate fertile rays, white sometimes pink when dried or lilac, corollas 5–8 mm
morphology.discs: Perfect fertile yellow florets with corollas 1.5–2 mm
morphology.fruits: Achenes ca. 1.5 mm, laterally flattened with 2 wings (ray fruits 3 wings); awns <1 mm or absent
morphology.habitat: Disturbed sites, pond margins and moist sand

source_disagreements: Contrast B. asteroides: ray corollas generally 8–15 mm, receptacles 6–10 mm and pappus awns about 1 mm.
